title: Bounded-limit preserving space-valued presheaves are filtered colimits of representables
statement:
Use the universes, infinite regular cardinals, $\kappa$-small simplicial sets and $\kappa$-filtered infinity categories of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and the spaces, coherent functors, transformations and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Small means in the fixed smaller universe $\mathcal U$; $\mathcal S$ is the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, let $A$ be a small infinity category admitting $\kappa$-small colimits, and put $\mathcal P(A)=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. Write $y:A\to\mathcal P(A)$ for $y(a)=\operatorname{Map}_A(-,a)$. For every $X\in\mathcal P(A)$ the following are equivalent:

(1) There exist a small $\kappa$-filtered infinity category $I$ and a coherent functor $p:I\to A$ such that $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{I}(y\circ p)$ in $\mathcal P(A)$.

(2) For every $\kappa$-small simplicial set $K$, every coherent diagram $q:K\to A$ and every colimiting cocone $\lambda:q\to\Delta_Ka$ in $A$, the map of spaces
$$X(a)\longrightarrow\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k)),$$
obtained by applying the contravariant functor $X$ to the components $\lambda_k:q(k)\to a$ together with their coherences, is an equivalence. The empty simplicial set $K=\varnothing$ is included: then $a$ is an initial object of $A$, the limit is a terminal space, and (2) requires $X(a)$ to be contractible.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, printed p. 404 (PDF page 422): equivalence of (1) and (3) when A admits kappa-small colimits. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks Project tag states this space-valued quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathcal P(A)$, which has small mapping spaces by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], and let $B\subset P$ be the full subcategory of objects equivalent to representables. The Yoneda functor is fully faithful by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] choose a coherent quasi-inverse $k:B\to A$, with counit $yk\simeq\mathrm{id}_B$. The target-fixed slice right fibration $P_{/X}\to P$ is classified by $\operatorname{Map}_P(-,X)$, by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Pull it back along $y$ and write $E=A\times_P P_{/X}\to A$. Its classifier is $a\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_P(y(a),X)\simeq X(a)$, naturally by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation]. The classification theorem permits a small right-fibration model $p:I\to A$ for this classifier since $A$ and all $X(a)$ are small. The equivalence of classifiers gives inverse maps with coherent inverse homotopies over $A$ between $I$ and $E$. In particular, their total quasicategories are equivalent. An object is a pair $(a,x)$ with $x\in X(a)$, and the corresponding arrow $y(a)\to X$ is given by Yoneda evaluation.

source.place: HTT Lemma 5.1.5.2 and Corollary 5.3.5.4 proof; smallness via straightening/unstraightening.

proof.text: Let $C=B\times_P P_{/X}$. The canonical source-projection cocone on $C$ has apex $X$ and is colimiting by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-representable-slice-density]. The projection $P_{/X}\to P$ is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Pulling back each horn-lifting problem shows that $\pi:C\to B$ is a right fibration as well; in particular $C$ is a quasicategory. Its opposite is a left fibration, since order reversal sends $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$. The target-prescribed equivalence-lifting clause of [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift], on opposites, makes $\pi$ an isofibration with the prescribed-source convention. All these categories are small in the larger ambient universe.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, category-of-elements proof, expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Since $y$ factors through $B$, the right fibration $E$ of step 1 is degreewise $A\times_B C$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-equivalence] to the equivalence $y:A\to B$ and the isofibration $\pi:C\to B$ from step 2. It gives the functor equivalence $r:E\to C$. This projection retains the $C$-coordinate, so its composite to $P$ is the diagram $yp_E$ and the arrow from that coordinate to $X$ is unchanged.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, category-of-elements proof, expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Reindex the canonical density cocone along $I\simeq E\xrightarrow{r}C$. Its canonical join form is part of [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-representable-slice-density]. Reindexing along an equivalence preserves its colimit property by clause (2) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], with the structure functor $P\to\Delta^0$. Indeed, the constant-test criterion [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] for this structure functor is precisely the ordinary colimiting cocone mapping-space criterion. The restricted cocone has diagram $yp$ and apex $X$, with components given by the fibre points of step 1; hence $X\simeq\operatorname{colim}_I yp$. Here $I$ is small, and no filteredness has yet been asserted.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, category-of-elements proof, expanded by the agent.

proof.text:
Assume (1), with small $\kappa$-filtered index $J$ and $t:J\to A$. For a $\kappa$-small $q:K\to A$ and colimiting cocone $\lambda:q\to\Delta_K a$, objectwise presheaf colimits (small colimits exist in $\mathcal S=\mathcal P(\Delta^0)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion]) and the contravariant representable colimit-to-limit property in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] give
$$X(a)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_A(a,t(j))\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_A(q(k),t(j)).$$
Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] to the coherent diagram $(k,j)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_A(q(k),t(j))$, the restriction of the coherent mapping bifunctor $H_A$ of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] along $q^{\mathrm{op}}\times t$, to obtain
$$X(a)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}_A(q(k),t(j))\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k)).$$
Taking opposites does not change the number of nondegenerate simplices, so $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ is still $\kappa$-small. Every comparison is induced by the legs of $\lambda$: after evaluation at $j,k$ it is precomposition by $q(k)\to a$. The naturality clauses of both cited statements retain these maps and coherences. Hence the displayed equivalence is exactly the specified comparison in (2). Both cited statements allow $K=\varnothing$.

source.place: HTT Corollary 5.3.5.4, (1) implies (3), using Proposition 5.1.2.2 and Proposition 5.3.3.3.

proof.text: For any small simplicial set $K$ and $q:K\to A$, put $F=Xq^{\mathrm{op}}$ and let $\Gamma_q$ be the section space of $q^*I\to K$. The dual mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies it with $\operatorname{Map}(\Delta *,F)$. More generally a map $T\to\Gamma_q$ is exactly a map $K\times T\to I$ over $q$, hence a coherent transformation $\Delta T\to F$ by the same classification formula. The limit exists by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], and the limiting-cone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] identifies these transformations with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,\lim F)$, naturally in $T$. Thus $\Gamma_q\simeq\lim F$, with the actual evaluation cone. This uses classification for arbitrary simplicial bases; it does not apply a section-limit theorem that assumes $K$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, category-of-elements proof, expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Let $\lambda:q\to\Delta_K a$ be a coherent cocone and $x\in X(a)$ a fibre point. The actual map $X(a)\to\lim Xq^{\mathrm{op}}$ induced by $X\lambda$ sends $x$ to the section with values $X(\lambda_k)(x)$ under step 6. By [lem-coef-infinity-section-cylinder-cocone], a path from a prescribed section $r$ to this section supplies a coherent cocone $r\to\Delta_K(a,x)$ in $I$ over the prescribed cylinder $\lambda:K\times\Delta^1\to A$. The lemma includes arbitrary simplicial $K$ and all parameter simplices.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.5.4, category-of-elements proof, expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Assume (2). For a $\kappa$-small diagram $r:K\to I$, let $q=pr$. By step 6, its section data correspond to a point $s\in\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k))$. By the hypothesis on $A$ choose a colimiting cocone $\lambda:q\to\Delta_K a$. Condition (2) makes the actual restriction map $X(a)\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(q(k))$ an equivalence. An inverse equivalence supplies a point $x\in X(a)$ and a path from its image to $s$, with all higher compatibility data. Step 7 makes these data a coherent cocone from $r$ to $(a,x)$ in $I$. For $K=\varnothing$, $a$ is initial, the limit is terminal, and (2) makes $X(a)$ contractible and in particular nonempty; this again gives a cocone. Thus every $\kappa$-small diagram in $I$ admits a cocone, precisely the definition of $\kappa$-filteredness in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category].

source.place: HTT Corollary 5.3.5.4, expanded proof of (3) implies (2), using the section calculation in step 4.

proof.text: The small index $I$ of step 1 is now $\kappa$-filtered by step 8. Its projection $p:I\to A$ and the colimiting fibre-point cocone from step 4 therefore give exactly the presentation required in (1). This proves (2) implies (1); step 5 proves the reverse implication.

lean.statement: theorem presheaf_ind_criterion (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : κ.IsRegular) (A : SSet.{u}) [SSet.Quasicategory A] (hA : ∀ (K : SSet.{u}), SSet.Presentability.IsKappaSmall κ K → ∀ (q : K ⟶ A), ∃ t : (coconeCategory q) _⦋0⦌, IsColimiting q t) (X : (infinityPresheaves A) _⦋0⦌) : ((∃ (I : SSet.{u}) (hI : SSet.Quasicategory I), SSet.Presentability.IsSmall.{u, u} I ∧ @SSet.Presentability.IsKappaFiltered κ I hI ∧ ∃ (p : I ⟶ A), ∃ t : (coconeCategory (SSet.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}.map p ≫ infinityYoneda A)) _⦋0⦌, IsColimiting (SSet.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}.map p ≫ infinityYoneda A) t ∧ ∃ e : (infinityPresheaves A) _⦋1⦌, IsEquivalenceEdge (infinityPresheaves A) e ∧ (infinityPresheaves A).δ 1 e = X ∧ (infinityPresheaves A).δ 0 e = t.1.1)) ↔ (∀ (K : SSet.{u}), SSet.Presentability.IsKappaSmall κ K → ∀ (q : K ⟶ A), ∀ (lam : (coconeCategory q) _⦋0⦌), IsColimiting q lam → IsPresheafLimitComparison X q lam)
lean.note: Uses the published presentability dependency. The induced-limit predicate fixes both the apex and the complete cylinder transformation obtained from the supplied cocone by taking opposites and applying the actual presheaf; no arbitrary limit cone is substituted.
